_comment: RA-010 tells the court and the other side that the filer will appear remotely. It comes into the packet on the filer's answer that they will, so item 1's Plaintiff/Petitioner box carries that answer's name and is ticked by it, and the name beside it is the filer's. Filed with the request, it meets the deadline page 3 gives the party asking for a protective-order hearing ('with the moving papers'). At filing the court has not yet set the hearing date - it does that on DV-109 - so item 2 explains that 'the whole case' needs no date; 'one hearing' asks for the date only when it is known. The Declaration of Notice on page 2 is not asked: it swears that notice was already given, which at filing it has not been, and the form lets a proof of service show it instead - the other side is told when this form is served on them with the rest of the papers. The caption is the packet's names; only the county and the courthouse branch are new. The questions after item 1's box are asked whenever the form is here; they follow that box only because it is printed first.

groups.question: Who else on your side will appear remotely?
groups.subtitle: Leave both unticked when it is only you.
labels: Someone else, such as a witness

groups.question: Do you want to appear remotely for the whole case or only at one hearing?
groups.subtitle: The court sets your hearing date after it reads your request, so the date is not known yet. Choosing the whole case means this one notice covers every hearing.

groups.question: How will you appear remotely?
groups.subtitle: The court's website says which ways its courtrooms allow.
labels: By phone or other audio only

person_asking_protection_name._why: The caption, item 1's name line and the page 2 caption print the filer's name, which DV-100 item 1 already asks under this name; the packet asks it once and this wording is for the form compiled on its own.

ra010_court_county.text: In which county is the court hearing your case?

court_street_address.text: What is the court's street address?
court_street_address._why: The caption's STREET ADDRESS line is the court address DV-100's caption already asks under this name; the packet asks it once.

ra010_court_branch_name.text: What is the name of the courthouse where your case is heard?
ra010_court_branch_name.subtitle: Some counties have several courthouses, called branches.

person_to_restrain_full_name.text: Who do you want protection from?
person_to_restrain_full_name._why: The DEFENDANT/RESPONDENT line of both captions is the person DV-100 item 2 names under this name; the packet asks it once.

appear_remotely_yes.text: Will you appear at your hearing remotely, by video or by phone?
appear_remotely_yes._why: Item 1's Plaintiff/Petitioner box is ticked exactly when the filer answers on DV-100 that they will appear remotely - the box carries that answer's name, so the packet never asks this; the wording is for the form compiled on its own.

ra010_proceeding_type.text: What kind of hearing is it?
ra010_proceeding_type.subtitle: For example: the hearing on my request for a domestic violence restraining order.

ra010_other_remote_aspects_requested.text: Do you want any other part of the hearing done remotely, such as a witness testifying by video?
ra010_other_remote_aspects_requested.subtitle: Item 4 is for hearings where people testify, and the hearing on a restraining order is one.

ra010_other_remote_aspects_description.text: Describe the parts of the hearing you want done remotely and the reasons for it.

ra010_agree_to_keep_confidential.text: Do you agree to keep the hearing as confidential as you would in the courtroom?

choices.question: Has the court set the date of that hearing?

continuations._why: Item 1's 'Other (name and role in case)' is ruled over two lines for one answer; a name and a role fit on the first.

The caption rules three lines for the court's address - street, mailing, city and ZIP. The packet holds the court's address as one answer (DV-100's caption box is 'Court name and street address'), and it prints whole on the street line, so the mailing and city lines are left as a filer leaves them when one line holds the address.

combines.question: Where can the court send you papers?
How can the court reach you?
What are your lawyer's State Bar number and law firm?
Who is the other person who will appear remotely?

fields.label: Their role in the case, such as witness

combines.question: When and where is that hearing?

ra010_attorney_for._why: The caption's ATTORNEY FOR (name) line names the party a lawyer represents - the filer - and is printed only when the filer has a lawyer. It is the filer's name, written while the lawyer answer is Yes.

ra010_lawyer_appears_remotely_name._why: Item 1's 'Attorney for Plaintiff/Petitioner (name)' is the lawyer's name, which DV-100 item 1 already asks; it prints only beside a ticked box, so a lawyer who is not appearing remotely is not named here.

autofill.why: The date beside the signature under item 5 has one correct answer and the form already knows it.
The typed name under the item 5 signature is the filer's, given in the caption.

alwaysShown.question: ra010_court_county
alwaysShown.why: The court's county in the caption is asked whether or not the filer has a lawyer; the lawyer question is the last of the filer's own block.

alwaysShown.question: ra010_others_appearing_remotely
alwaysShown.why: RA-010 is in the packet only because the filer said they will appear remotely, so the rest of item 1 is asked whenever the form is here. It follows item 1's first box only because that box is printed first.

alwaysShown.question: ra010_appear_by
alwaysShown.why: Item 3, how the filer will appear, is asked whether or not item 2's hearing date is known; it follows item 2 only because item 2 is printed first.

alwaysShown.question: ra010_agree_to_keep_confidential
alwaysShown.why: Item 5 is asked whatever the answer to item 4; it follows item 4 only because it is printed after it.
